subject: cfa seemingly constraining loadings/intercepts between groups by default

messages.author: c4e2eecf692f530f
messages.subject: cfa seemingly constraining loadings/intercepts between groups by default
parts:
I've noticed that when I try to conduct a measurement invariance analysis using measurementInvariance() (from semTools), Model 1 seems to constrain the loadings and intercepts between groups, yielding an identical result to model 3.  If I take a step back and simply try to fit what would be Model 1 using cfa(), I obtain the same results as with the measurementInvariance function, so I think something is weird with the way R is running the cfa function on my data.

I have 21 observed variables (S1-S21) in two groups (coded 2 and 4 in the "group" column in my dataset, which is dataF13ExpAll).
EFAmodel is defined based on exploratory factor analysis of a previous dataset:

EFAmodel <- '

    f1 =~ S1 + S3 + S4

    f2 =~ S6 + S7 + S8 + S9 + S10

    f3 =~ S11 + S12 + S13 + S14 

    f4 =~ S15 + S16 + S17

    f5 =~ S18 + S19 + S20 + S21

    f6 =~ S2 + S5

'

When I enter
MItest <- measurementInvariance(model = EFAmodel, data = dataF13ExpAll, estimator = "MLM", mimic = "Mplus", group = "group")
#incomplete cases have been previously removed from the data

Taking a step back and simply trying to fit what would be Model 1 in the measurementInvariance output:
I enter
fitTest <- cfa(model = EFAmodel, data = dataF13ExpAll, estimator = "MLM", mimic = "Mplus", group = "group")
> summary(fitTest, estimates = FALSE, fit.measures = TRUE)

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: cfa seemingly constraining loadings/intercepts between groups by default
parts:
On 11/19/2013 05:25 AM, Mary Beth Anzovino wrote:
> I've noticed that when I try to conduct a measurement invariance
> analysis using measurementInvariance() (from semTools), Model 1 seems to
> constrain the loadings and intercepts between groups,

> MItest <- measurementInvariance(model = EFAmodel, data = dataF13ExpAll,
> estimator = "MLM", mimic = "Mplus", group = "group")

The issue is the mimic="Mplus" flag. If we 'mimic' Mplus, the
intercepts+loadings are always constrained to be equal across groups...

Solution: remove the mimic="Mplus" flag.

(Was there a specific reason you needed mimic="Mplus"?)


Yves.
